questions.question: Define the term 'balanced government budget'. (2 marks)
A government collects $228bn in tax revenue and spends $260bn. Calculate its budget balance and state whether it is a deficit or a surplus. (2 marks)
Explain how an increase in government spending affects aggregate demand. (4 marks)
Draw an AD/AS diagram to show the effect of a $16bn increase in government spending on an economy with an upward-sloping short-run aggregate supply curve. (4 marks)
Analyse how an increase in a central bank's policy interest rate reduces the rate of inflation. (6 marks)
Examine the case for an independent central bank setting interest rates rather than the government. (8 marks)

A worker receives $200 a week in benefits. They are offered a job paying $250 a week. Benefits are withdrawn at 80 cents for every dollar earned, and income tax of 10% is paid on the wage. Calculate the increase in the worker's weekly income from taking the job, and the effective marginal deduction rate. (4 marks)
Discuss whether interventionist supply-side policies are more effective than free-market supply-side policies in raising an economy's productive capacity. (14 marks)
Explain why an economy with an inflation rate above that of its trading partners may develop a current account deficit. (4 marks)
Evaluate whether a government should prioritise low inflation over low unemployment. (20 marks)
